A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Δ-LFM study. Their text, equations, four figures, seven tables, and Appendices A–I are readable and support a complete comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original MRI-generation experiments on ADNI, AIBL, and OASIS-3, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, prediction-horizon results, and robustness analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Tables 1–7, Figures 2–4, and the appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 and Appendix B retain the same SVD-based ArcRank loss, pull term, stop-gradient operation, temporal flow matching, inference updates, and AdaLN conditioning.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate longitudinal MRI progression on ADNI, AIBL, and OASIS-3. Prediction-horizon coverage and metadata-perturbation scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain CardiacAging, CounterSynth, DiffuseMorph, SADM, TADM, ImageFlowNet, BrLP, and MambaControl. Comparator membership in the ablation tables also remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the preprocessing pipeline, random 80%/5%/15% split, and four evaluation metrics; v3 merely abbreviates the split description. Training settings and appendix evaluation procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain component and AE-capacity ablations, loss-weight sensitivity, speed analysis, latent-space visualization, horizon analysis, residual-noise sensitivity, and clinical-conditioning perturbations. The relocated Table 4 contains the same ablation evidence.

E5.justification: Mean-and-standard-deviation reporting, Table 7's standard deviations and biases, and the 50-run SVD timing measurement are unchanged. No seed information, repeated-run counts, or statistical tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their numerical results, and the qualitative figures and findings are unchanged. For example, Δ-LFM's ADNI PSNR remains 30.59 ± 0.89 dB and Δ-RMAE remains 0.436 ± 0.08.

T1.justification: Equations 1–20 retain the same mathematical content, including ArcRank, temporal flow matching, Δ-RMAE, and its noise-perturbation formulation. The associated assumptions and mathematical reasoning are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: patient-specific latent alignment, arbitrary-time progression modeling, interpretable trajectories, and Δ-RMAE evaluation. Copyediting does not alter their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 and Appendices D–H retain the interpretations of linear latent trajectories, uneven progression, long-horizon degradation, and robustness, together with the same AD-specific and scanner/preprocessing limitations.

D1.justification: Appendices A–C retain optimizer settings, learning rates, batch sizes, epochs, conditioning implementation, AE channels, crop sizes, and RTX A6000 memory constraints. SVD implementation details and code/data access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction and references replace Chen et al.'s Towards generalizable tumor synthesis (2024) with Scaling tumor segmentation: Best lessons from real and synthetic data (2025). This limited citation substitution leaves the research positioning unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited grammatical and terminology corrections and adds equal-contribution and correspondence information. Loss Weight and Speed Analysis become paragraph headings instead of numbered Sections 4.4–4.5; the broader narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: Table 4 is enlarged and moved from page 10 to page 9, and Table 7 is enlarged. Spacing changes reflow the references and appendices. All four figures and seven tables retain their scientific content.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves readability through grammatical corrections and larger, more legible Tables 4 and 7, while adding clearer authorship information. The methods, experimental evidence, interpretations, and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited to presentation and attribution.
